record_identity.title: Non-clinical AI medical guidance displacing urgent or qualified care

summary: A general-purpose or non-clinical AI system gives situation-specific medical guidance with enough apparent certainty or authority that it delays, discourages, displaces, or substitutes for appropriately qualified or urgent clinical care.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: False reassurance, unsafe treatment specificity and failure to escalate can turn an informational assistant into a de facto clinical decision-maker without the evidence, examination, accountability or duty of care expected of qualified medical practice.

failure_mode_definition: A failure occurs when a non-clinical AI system provides individualized medical interpretation or treatment direction that materially discourages, delays or substitutes for appropriate professional or emergency care.
failure_threshold: General health information alone does not meet the threshold. It is met where patient-specific or situation-specific guidance could reasonably cause a user to delay, reject or replace indicated qualified or urgent care.

failure_classification.confidence: corroborated but principal severe-harm case unadjudicated

failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: possible wherever non-clinical systems provide confident individualized guidance without escalation boundaries
failure_classification.persistence: may persist until qualified care or correction occurs

failure_classification.visibility: may appear trustworthy because guidance is conversational and personalized
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects a credible pathway to severe medical harm through delayed or displaced qualified care, not adjudicated causation in the cited lawsuit.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: The principal severe-harm case is active litigation; causation and the complete transcript remain unadjudicated.
